title: "Linguistic Feature Distributions and LMd Associations"
output: html_notebook

## Setup

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)

# Use the same paths and feature variant as the upstream analysis scripts.
results_dir <- Sys.getenv("FHS_RESULTS_DIR", unset = "Results")
data_dir <- Sys.getenv("FHS_OUTPUT_DIR", unset = file.path(results_dir, "Data"))
feature_variant <- tolower(Sys.getenv("FHS_FEATURE_VARIANT", unset = "normal"))
if (!(feature_variant %in% c("normal", "filtered"))) {
  stop("FHS_FEATURE_VARIANT must be 'normal' or 'filtered'.")
}

input_feature_filename <- if (feature_variant == "filtered") {
  "feature_np_tau_amyloid_filtered_20251116.csv"
} else {
  "feature_np_tau_amyloid_20251116.csv"
}
input_rds_filename <- if (feature_variant == "filtered") {
  "tauFeatureAmyloidDemo_filtered.rds"
} else {
  "tauFeatureAmyloidDemo.rds"
}

table_dir <- file.path(results_dir, if (feature_variant == "filtered") {
  "Table_Results_filtered"
} else {
  "Table_Results"
})
figure_dir <- file.path(results_dir, if (feature_variant == "filtered") {
  "Figure_Results_filtered"
} else {
  "Figure_Results"
})
# Preserve the original filtered histogram output directory; keep normal plots separate.
distribution_dir <- if (feature_variant == "filtered") {
  file.path(results_dir, "Figure_Results", "Feature_Distribution_Filtered")
} else {
  file.path(results_dir, "Figure_Results", "Feature_Distribution")
}
for (path in c(table_dir, figure_dir, distribution_dir)) {
  dir.create(path, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
}
```

## Feature distributions

```{r}
# Data Link output: the original filtered histogram script used columns 63:120.
# The normal feature table has two fewer feature columns in the corresponding range.
whole_df <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, input_feature_filename))
hist_cols <- if (feature_variant == "filtered") 63:120 else 63:118
if (ncol(whole_df) < max(hist_cols)) {
  stop("The linked feature table has fewer columns than expected for the selected variant.")
}
```

```{r}
# Save one histogram per selected feature, using the original hist_<feature>.png filenames.
for (i in hist_cols) {
  
  colname <- colnames(whole_df)[i]
  values <- whole_df[[i]]

  outfile <- file.path(distribution_dir, paste0("hist_", colname, ".png"))
  
  png(outfile, width = 1000, height = 600, res = 150)
  
  hist(values,
       main = paste("Histogram of", colname),
       xlab = colname,
       col = "skyblue",
       border = "white")
  
  dev.off()
}
```

## LMd associations with linguistic features

```{r}
# Input from the corresponding speech-marker analysis (normal or filtered).
whole_df <- readRDS(file.path(data_dir, input_rds_filename))
```

### Model 1: LMd as the only predictor

For each linguistic feature, fit `feature ~ LMd` (the feature is the response).

```{r}
lm_featureLmd <- data.frame(
  Feature = character(),
  Estimate = numeric(),
  StdError = numeric(),
  tValue = numeric(),
  Pr = numeric(),
  Model = character(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
for (c in colnames(whole_df[,8:61])){
  formular_1<-as.formula(paste(c, "~ LMd"))
  model_1<-lm(formular_1,data=whole_df)
  coef_table_1<-coef(summary(model_1))
  for (var in rownames(coef_table_1)[-1]) {
    var_coef <- coef_table_1[var,]
    lm_featureLmd <- rbind(lm_featureLmd, data.frame(
      Feature = var,
      Estimate = var_coef["Estimate"],
      StdError = var_coef["Std. Error"],
      tValue = var_coef["t value"],
      Pr = var_coef["Pr(>|t|)"],  
      Model = c
    ))
  }
}
```

### Model 2: LMd with demographic and amyloid covariates

For each linguistic feature, fit `feature ~ LMd + age + sex + Educg + ADNI.petpos`.

```{r}
lm_featureLmd_2 <- data.frame(
  Feature = character(),
  Estimate = numeric(),
  StdError = numeric(),
  tValue = numeric(),
  Pr = numeric(),
  Model = character(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
for (c in colnames(whole_df[,8:61])){
  formular_2<-as.formula(paste(c, "~ LMd + age+sex+Educg+ADNI.petpos"))
  model_2<-lm(formular_2,data=whole_df)
  coef_table_2<-coef(summary(model_2))
  for (var in rownames(coef_table_2)[2]) {
    var_coef <- coef_table_2[var,]
    lm_featureLmd_2 <- rbind(lm_featureLmd_2, data.frame(
      Feature = var,
      Estimate = var_coef["Estimate"],
      StdError = var_coef["Std. Error"],
      tValue = var_coef["t value"],
      Pr = var_coef["Pr(>|t|)"],  
      Model = c
    ))
  }
}
```

### Compare regression estimates

```{r}
# Align the two model results by feature name; retain the original comparison columns.
feature_lmd_coef<-merge(lm_featureLmd,lm_featureLmd_2,by='Model')
feature_lmd_coef_sel<-feature_lmd_coef[,c("Model", "Pr.x","Pr.y",'Estimate.x','Estimate.y')]
feature_lmd_coef_sel$sig<-ifelse(feature_lmd_coef_sel$Pr.x<0.05 & feature_lmd_coef_sel$Pr.y<0.05,'TRUE',"FALSE")

# The source notebook wrote a cluster-annotated table; that external cluster
# analysis is intentionally excluded, so save the unclustered comparison explicitly.
write.csv(feature_lmd_coef, file.path(table_dir, "Feature_LMd_regression_comparison.csv"))
```

```{r}
# Compare unadjusted and adjusted LMd regression coefficients.
p<-ggplot(feature_lmd_coef_sel, aes(x = Estimate.x, y = Estimate.y, color = sig)) +
  geom_point(size = 1) +  
  scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" = "black")) +  
  # geom_hline(yintercept = abs(log(0.05)), linetype = "dashed", color = "blue") +  
  # geom_vline(xintercept = abs(log(0.05)), linetype = "dashed", color = "blue") +  
  theme_minimal() +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "green")+
  labs(title = "Scatter Plot of p-values",
       x = "Feature LMd Estimate",
       y = "Feature LMd controled Estimate",
       color = "Significant") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")+
  geom_text_repel(
    data = subset(feature_lmd_coef_sel, Pr.x< 0.05 & Pr.y <0.05), 
    aes(label = Model),  
    size = 3,              
    max.overlaps = 25,    
    box.padding = 0.5,     
    point.padding = 0.3
  )
p
```

```{r}
ggsave(file.path(figure_dir, "feature_lmd_scatterplot_estimate.png"), plot = p, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```
